blocks.text: Communicating results and conclusions is an important step in data analysis and research. It helps readers understand what the data shows and what decisions can be made, so that results are not misunderstood or misused. Findings should be explained simply and logically, and conclusions must rest strictly on the analysed data. Good communication improves transparency and credibility and supports future research.

items: Interpreting test results: understand what the statistical outcomes (p-values, confidence levels, test statistics) mean, decide whether the hypothesis is supported, and consider the context of the data; misinterpretation leads to wrong conclusions.
Presenting findings clearly: organise results logically, support them with tables, charts and graphs, use simple language instead of jargon, and highlight the key points.

Connecting conclusions to hypotheses: state clearly whether each original hypothesis is supported, justify this with the data and test results, and keep personal opinion out of the conclusion. This completes the research process.
